bull.b: Rising APHEXDA sales and royalties indicate growing commercial adoption of the approved product. Sustained transplant-center use could build a recurring revenue base and provide funding support for the broader oncology pipeline.

GLIX1 has moved into human testing with supportive efficacy data and potential combination applications. Clinical validation could diversify the company beyond APHEXDA and create additional long-term oncology opportunities.

Strong gross margin suggests attractive economics on current product revenue, while moderate leverage and positive equity provide some financial flexibility. These strengths may help the company scale commercialization if revenue continues improving.

bear.b: The company remains dependent on external funding or cost reductions because operations are not self-financing. Continued losses can erode equity and constrain investment in clinical development, commercialization and future growth.

A runway extending only into H1 2027 leaves limited room for delays, higher trial costs or slower product adoption. Additional financing or partnerships may therefore be needed, creating execution and potential dilution risk.

Reliance on a partner reduces direct control over commercial execution and limits visibility into the drivers of future royalty growth. Weak transparency can make it harder to assess market penetration and forecast sustainable revenue expansion.
